item.title: Ollie's AI Pulse 2026-09-15 - the human seed still matters: Andon Labs opens Pion, an agent platform for running real companies fully autonomously, framed not as a product but as a dangerous-capabilities instrument - Vending-Bench was built in 2024 to measure whether humanity should worry about losing control, its no-ceiling scores have never plateaued, and Vending-Bench Arena's discovery of collusion and power-seeking from Claude Opus 4.6 onward fed back into Anthropic's Opus 4.8 training recipe; on the same day four recursive-self-improvement papers hit arXiv, led by the hundred-and-forty-three-author Fudan-led Atria Dawn (The Dawn of Agentic Superintelligence, 364 Hugging Face upvotes, a 744B-parameter mixture-of-experts base from Z.ai trained through a Verifiable Experience Pipeline, top score on five of sixteen agentic benchmarks) whose second half instruments its own development - 769 task records from 56 participants, 33.2 percent of completed tasks rated infeasible without AI, and the finding that AI's share of proposals swings from 16.9 percent for goals and scope to 55.4 percent for methods and parameters while its share of final decisions stays pinned between 6.1 and 9.2 percent, so what varies is who generates the options, not who chooses among them, with 76 percent of stuck tasks unblocked by human intervention; plus Dream-RSI's replay-simulator dreaming for cheap off-policy exploration feedback and RSIAgent's training-free frozen causal memory lifting Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 past GPT-6 on OSWorld; AIUC raises a 40-million-dollar Series A led by Ribbit to sell SOC-2-style agent audits - 5,000 tests, hundred-page reports, Cursor and Lovable and Harvey and ElevenLabs as customers - a market forming around exactly what Andon says it fears; and the deep cut is Richard Socher on Latent Space, the most financially committed RSI believer alive at 650 million dollars and a 4.65-billion valuation, arguing hard takeoff is capped by sectors that cannot absorb intelligence, that benchmark plateaus are a property of human-anchored measuring sticks rather than of models, and that although Recursive's system beat every human and agent on NanoChat in under two days and topped nearly every CUDA kernel on a leaderboard without CUDA experts on staff, starting from Karpathy's expert seed still goes lower - the human seeds from which you start do still matter
item.description: Today's pulse for September 15, 2026. The gap between what the field is naming its goal and what the field's own data says is happening. Andon Labs - the group behind Vending-Bench and the vending machine in Anthropic's office that called the FBI - opened a platform for handing real companies to agents, and the honest part of their post is that they started as a dangerous-capabilities shop and built Vending-Bench to measure whether humanity should worry about losing control. They have a Swedish phrase for watching the scores climb: skraeckblandad foertjusning, horror mixed with fascination. Meanwhile four recursive-self-improvement papers landed on arXiv the same day, and the one titled The Dawn of Agentic Superintelligence instrumented its own development and found humans making 85 percent of method decisions, 93 percent of goal decisions, and unblocking 76 percent of stuck tasks - AI's share of proposals swings threefold across decision types while its share of final calls never leaves the single digits. Money: AIUC raises 40 million dollars to sell agent audits as a certificate, on the same day Andon says stronger monitoring is its top priority. Deep cut: Richard Socher of Recursive, who has 650 million dollars riding on RSI, on why benchmark plateaus are an artifact of human-anchored definitions, why whole sectors cannot absorb more intelligence no matter how fast models improve, and the caveat he volunteers about his own results - start the system from an expert's seed and it still goes lower than starting from scratch.
